Health Assessment

Health assessment — purposes, methods, physical examination and documentation.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • State the purposes of health assessment
  • Describe methods of assessment
  • Demonstrate a basic physical examination

In simple words

Health assessment is the systematic collection of information about a patient’s health. It is the first step of the nursing process and guides all nursing care.

Assessment gives a baseline, identifies health problems and helps plan care. It is continuous throughout hospitalization.

Methods of assessment

Method What it is Example
Inspection Looking Skin colour, wounds
Palpation Feeling Pulse, tenderness
Percussion Tapping Lung density
Auscultation Listening Heart and bowel sounds

Components

  • Health history — present illness, past history, family history, lifestyle.
  • Physical examination — head to toe, systematic.
  • Vital signs — temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure, SpO2.
  • Psychosocial — mood, support, coping, culture.

🔴 Assessment guides all care

Health assessment is the foundation of the nursing process. It identifies problems and guides planning, implementation and evaluation.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Admission — do a full head-to-toe assessment and record baseline findings.
  • Every shift — assess vital signs and any change in condition.
  • Before procedures — assess to plan and to compare afterwards.
  • Deteriorating patient — reassess frequently and report changes early.
  • Documentation — record findings factually, with date, time and signature.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Health assessment is the systematic collection of health information.
  2. It is the first step of the nursing process.
  3. Four methods: inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation.
  4. Components: health history, physical examination, vital signs, psychosocial.
  5. Assessment is continuous, not only on admission.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Inspection is usually done first.
  2. Palpation uses the hands; percussion taps; auscultation uses a stethoscope.
  3. Vital signs: temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure, SpO2.
  4. Head-to-toe examination is systematic.

📌 Memory trick

Methods: “IPPA” — Inspection, Palpation, Percussion, Auscultation. Say “ipp-ah”.

60-second revision

  • Assessment = systematic health information collection.
  • First step of nursing process.
  • Methods: IPPA — inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation.
  • Components: history, exam, vital signs, psychosocial.
  • Continuous, head-to-toe, systematic.

Test yourself

The first step of the nursing process is:

Answer: B. Assessment is the first step of the nursing process.

Which assessment method uses a stethoscope?

Answer: D. Auscultation means listening, usually with a stethoscope.

Inspection means:

Answer: B. Inspection is looking at the patient.

Vital signs include all except:

Answer: C. Height is not a vital sign.

Assessment should be done:

Answer: B. Assessment is continuous throughout the patient’s stay.
